Title: September 7, 2023 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
Overview: The Boulder City Council opened with declarations (flood anniversary, National Voter Registration Day, Suicide Prevention Month) and open comment, then approved the consent agenda, including a resolution supporting LGBTQ+ access to public accommodations. The council heard extensive public testimony and accepted the Reimagine Policing Plan and disbanded its subcommittee unanimously. It also received a staff update on inclusionary housing changes, with direction to pursue cash-in-lieu restructuring, reduced on-site requirements, and a possible linkage fee study.

Topic1.Title: Declarations and Announcements
Topic1.Summary: Council read declarations recognizing the 10th anniversary of the 2013 Front Range flood, National Voter Registration Day on September 19, and National Suicide Prevention Month. Rise Against Suicide's Jenna Carr and Lauren spoke in appreciation of the recognition. Staff also announced the What's Up Boulder event and the Better Public Meetings scorecard.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Public Testimony
Topic2.Summary: Residents spoke on the proposed Boulder Airport closure, police oversight and officer conduct, the hill commercial area liquor regulations, and bear activity and trash in the University Hill area. Other speakers raised South Boulder maintenance concerns and homelessness camp proposals. Council members and staff responded and committed to follow-ups.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda items 3a through 3i unanimously. Item 3h concerned a planning matter with a second reading scheduled for September 21 and possible third reading. Item 3i was Resolution 1339 supporting LGBTQ+ people's access to goods, services, and public accommodations without discrimination in light of the 303 Creative decision.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up Check-In for 1345 28th Street
Topic4.Summary: Council considered calling up a site review for three student housing apartment buildings at 1345 28th Street. No member requested a call-up, so the item proceeded with planning board review.

Topic5.Title: Reimagine Policing Plan Public Hearing
Topic5.Summary: Chief Maris Harold, Wendy Schwarz, and Robin Engel of the National Policing Institute presented the Reimagine Policing Plan, which emphasizes problem-solving policing, holistic governance, staffing aligned to the ICMA rule of 60, and accountability metrics. Staff noted that the funding requests would come through future budget cycles. Council and speakers largely supported the plan, though some residents raised concerns about downtown crime and staffing levels.

Topic6.Title: Public Testimony on Reimagine Policing
Topic6.Summary: Speakers representing business groups, neighborhood associations, and residents voiced strong support for the plan, citing crime on Pearl Street and in the downtown area. Some speakers called for more police staffing and criticized council decisions and the police oversight panel. Others urged equity and community engagement in implementation.

Topic7.Title: Council Discussion and Vote on Reimagine Policing
Topic7.Summary: Council members praised the community engagement process and the work of the subcommittee. Several members stressed that the plan is a roadmap requiring ongoing implementation and accountability. Council then approved a motion to accept the plan and disband the subcommittee by roll call vote, unanimously.

Topic8.Title: Inclusionary Housing Program Update
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented proposed updates to the inclusionary housing program, including moving cash-in-lieu to a per-square-foot basis, reducing the on-site for-sale requirement from 25% to 15%, and exploring a Nexus study for a linkage fee on demolitions and large additions. Kaiser Marston's feasibility analysis found developers consistently choose cash-in-lieu over on-site units. Council members expressed concern about trading on-site middle-income units for more off-site rental units, but supported the code cleanups and continued analysis.
